articles.excerpt: After having this spot saved on Google Maps for quite some time, I took my bike and cycled all the way to Biesenthal and it was worthwhile indeed.

blocks.content:
I got a little special interest in artsy, dreamy and whimsical museums. The closer they are to nature and interesting landscapes, the better. I stumbled across Wehmühle some years ago, put it on my Google Maps "to visit" list and never got there. This year, there was a substantial itch and I finally needed to go there, as my Instagram algorithm pushed this place on me multiple times. As I do not have a car, I had to go there by bicycle. This worked out kinda fine and after surviving the Berlin traffic and finding my way through a grey-ist north-eastern Berlin, I cycled along fields, lakes, the Autobahn and finally found Wehrmuehle at the end of a forest path.

It grew on me very quickly. Loved the curation of the different artworks and especially the transcendence from the art space to the local nature reserve. It felt really remote and far away from the usual Berlin noise. After a Campari Spritz and a piece of apple pie, I returned and I definitely need to come back sooner than later.

articles.title: a visit to wehrmuehle

articles.excerpt: I pushed myself to do some photowalks after regular 9-5 duty and between weekend relaxation and came across some interesting perspectives and berlin summer vibes.

blocks.content:
As this is the first article, I am sharing on this little blog, a short introduction may be worthwhile. In addition to the usual instagram spam, I would like to set up a little outlet for sharing my photography and related thoughts. There will be a strong Berlin focus, but other locations and places will follow. 

To have an easy start, I would like to share a quick recap of august 2026 photowalks, which led me to summery Kreuzberg, Hansaviertel and Mitte.

slides.caption: stopping by the notorious voo store
and having some spectacular lighting at Kotti

blocks.content: I know Berlin is multifaceted and there is not one specific Berlin, but a summery evening in Kreuzberg is one of the most Berlin things. Hanging out next to Landwehrkanal, strolling along Reichenberger Str. or having a drink at the usual suspects like Ankerklause - there is a certain magic.

slides.caption: scenery with some Oscar Niemeyer in the background

blocks.content:
I stumbled upon Hansaviertel two years ago on Instagram after overseeing this place for quite some time. And now I am kinda obsessed with the architecture and I found myself a new favorite café at the heart of it. Is this location spectacular or mind boggling - certainly not, but I like the modernism and I am into the idea, that this was built with a certain vision in mind.

To conclude the recap I got some snapshots of Mitte Mitte. Is this area a bit snobby and performative - yes. But it is still a cute little microcosm and always offers some nice motives and perspectives.

articles.title: august photo recap

articles.excerpt: Continuing my series about cute little museums, I took the U3 to southwest Berlin and went to Haus am Waldsee. In close proximity to Grunewald and Krumme Lanke, there is a museum which kinda hit all the spots - excellent curation, nice interior, whimsical outdoor are and a very good café.

blocks.content:
My relationship to southwest Berlin is a bit ambiguous. On the one hand, I was very glad moving out of this part of the city after living there for nearly four years. The long bus and S-Bahn rides were a pain in the ass and I never felt truly at home. In addition, it is a part of West-Berlin which does not really resonate with me. Steglitz looks a bit like an average West-German town and like Charlottenburg it seems to be a completely different world. In a way it is very much Berlin but at the same time it is not (at least from my point of view). But on the other hand, it is indeed very special how Berlin slowly transcends from metropolis to forests, lakes and nature in general.

An of course there are some (hidden) gems like the Liebermann Villa on the shores of Wannsee, there is the Brücke Museum, the Mexikoplatz, Krumme Lanke and Schlachtensee, Pfaueninsel and Haus am Waldsee. The latter is one of my favorite museums in Berlin due to the extraordinary combination of curation, interior, exterior and café. It ticks all the boxes. I came across this place 3 years ago in the context of 2023 Berlin Art Week and was immediately enchanted. Even though it is quite popular, the atmosphere remains very intimate and in my view this strengthens the experience of the displayed artworks. I am also a big fan of its niche and bespoke curations. 10/10 will always recommend ;-)

slides.caption: full view of the historic building

articles.title: southwest berlin whimsy
